1.title: Understand greenhouse gas conversion
1.intro: These machines capture or convert gases such as carbon dioxide or methane into fuels, chemicals or solids.
pts: Know the main routes: capture and store, convert to fuel, convert to materials, burn-off of methane.
Learn the numbers: tonnes captured per year, energy used per tonne, cost per tonne.
Buyers: industrial plants, landfills, farms, energy firms, municipalities.
Pick one source gas and one buyer type.
1.ex: Landfill gas contains about half methane; capturing and converting 1,000 t of methane avoids about 25,000 t carbon-dioxide equivalent over 100 years.
1.act: Write a one-page problem statement with source, gas, volume and buyer.

2.title: Know environmental and safety rules
pts: Federal and provincial environmental law set emission limits and reporting.
Pressure vessels and gas systems follow technical safety codes and need certified welders and inspectors.
Carbon credits and offsets need approved methods and verifiers.
Permits for installation and operation come before building.
2.ex: Row: 'Operate a gas conversion unit | provincial environment ministry | permit and monitoring plan | before start-up | permit on file'.
2.act: Build a rules table for a landfill pilot.

3.title: Design a small conversion unit
3.intro: Start with mass and energy balance.
pts: Draw block diagram: inlet gas, clean-up, reactor, product, vent.
Calculate mass in = mass out for one hour.
Choose sensors for flow, temperature, pressure and gas composition.
Plan safety: shut-offs, leak detection, venting.
3.ex: Inlet 100 kg per hour gas; product 62 kg; vent 4 kg; unaccounted 34 kg → investigate leak or measurement.
3.act: Complete a balance for a chosen design.

4.title: Cost the machine and the tonne
4.intro: Customers buy cost per tonne avoided.
pts: Capital cost spread over years of life.
Operating cost: power, catalysts, labour, maintenance.
Revenue: product sales and credits.
Break-even and payback.
4.ex: Machine 640,000 over 10 years = 64,000 a year; operating 150,000; capacity 5,000 t... teaching cost 43 per tonne. Compare with the credit price. Teaching figures in CAD.
4.act: Compute cost per tonne and payback.

5.title: Operate, measure and verify
pts: Install calibrated meters.
Log inputs and outputs daily.
Arrange third-party verification.
Maintenance schedule and spares.
5.ex: Monthly report: captured 410 t; uptime 92%; verified by auditor.
5.act: Keep a 4-week data log with calibration dates.

6.title: Win a pilot site
pts: Approach site managers with data.
Offer pilot with shared cost.
Show permits and safety plan.
Align with their climate targets.
6.act: Pitch a pilot to three sites.

7.title: Manage safety, claims and community
pts: Hazard review before start-up.
Claims backed by verified data.
Consult neighbours and communities.
Emergency plan.
7.ex: Risk: 'Gas leak | 2 x 5 | detectors and shutoff | site lead | weekly test'.

8.title: Pilot and scale
pts: Run 90 days.
Compare cost per tonne with plan.
Stop rule: uptime under 70% means fix.
Plan manufacturing.

quiz: Mass in equals mass out; gaps show leaks or errors.
Annual cost divided by tonnes avoided.
Flow and gas composition (or temperature, pressure).
Trust and permits depend on it.
Capital divided by yearly net gain.
